Makes call recording more resistant to interruptions.

Android can stop CallVault's background helper at any time. With this on, a recording already in progress is no longer affected when that happens.

Off by default — you can also turn it on later in Settings ▸ Reliability.
Resilient recording is on. A recording already in progress is no longer affected if Android stops CallVault\'s background helper.
Your setup, checked by your own calls
Settings in a panel, and calls that record more reliably

Settings now slides in over the app instead of replacing it, grouped so each screen is a short list rather than everything at once. Recordings show when the call happened and how long it lasted.\n\nUnderneath: several ways a recording could be lost or spoiled have been fixed, including crackly audio with Resilient recording, and one side going missing from VoIP calls on Samsung phones.
Recording that recovers on its own

A rare stall in the connection to the recorder could leave recording silently switched off until the app was restarted — with nothing on screen to say so. It now times out and recovers by itself.\n\nYou can also choose when recordings upload to Drive: immediately, daily or weekly. Find it under Settings ▸ Storage, together with Retention, which has moved into the same section.

The status card now tells you whether recording actually worked, based on your real calls rather than a green light that only means the app started. If a call was not recorded, it says so and why — a folder that was never set, Developer options switched off, a permission lost to an update.\n\nAlso: CallVault now speaks Brazilian Portuguese, and every other language has been brought up to date.

Turning on USB debugging lets CallVault switch Wireless debugging off and keep it off. No cable is needed, and unlike Wireless debugging it opens no network port — so it is the safer of the two to leave on. Optional: recording works either way.\n\nAlso fixed: turning USB debugging off could leave CallVault unable to record, without saying so.

On some phones CallVault could keep switching Wireless debugging on and off without ever becoming ready to record. That is fixed. Where Wireless debugging is the only way in, CallVault now leaves it on and tells you which setting would let it be switched off again.\n\nAlso fixed: an app call could report a failure even though it recorded fine, and could be labelled with the wrong app.

CallVault can now record calls made inside apps like WhatsApp, Signal and Telegram — both sides of the conversation, not just your own voice. Recordings show which app the call was made in, and the contact\'s name when the app provides it.\n\nExperimental: it works with some apps and not others, and an app can block recording at any time in an update.

Android can stop CallVault\'s background helper at any time, which used to cut a recording short and leave you with half a call. With this on, a recording already under way carries on to the end regardless.
Keep recording when the screen locks
On many phones, locking the screen during a call was stopping the recorder mid-call. That is fixed, and CallVault now warns you if your phone\'s USB setting is the one causing it.

Faster to open, and quieter about problems that are not there

Opening CallVault is quick again, and stays quick however many calls you keep. 2.2.0 re-read the length of every recording each time the list was drawn, so once you had a few dozen calls the list was slow enough that a call recorded minutes earlier could look as though it had never been recorded at all.

The warning that recordings had stopped reaching Google Drive no longer appears when they have not stopped. Two people were told their backup had failed while every recording was arriving perfectly well.

The headings inside an exported transcript, the number of selected apps and the back button now follow the language you have chosen instead of staying in English. The debug report can also say which app is holding the microphone, for a problem that is proving hard to catch.
Find a call again, and steer one while it happens

Mark a moment while you are still talking. A button on the call notification drops a bookmark where you press it, and the recording shows them as chips that play from there — on phone calls and app calls alike. App calls have controls at all now: pause, resume, stop and mark, where before one could only be started and finished.

Finding a call again is easier: star the ones worth keeping, label them with your own words, and search across summaries and your own notes rather than only the spoken words. Transcripts export as text, Markdown, SRT, VTT or JSON.

CallVault also speaks up when it has quietly stopped working — if recording cannot start after a reboot, or recordings stop reaching Drive. Both used to be silent. New housekeeping can cap how much space recordings take or drop very short ones. It is all off by default, and a starred recording is never deleted automatically.
Settings ▸ Storage ▸ Retention for the housekeeping options

Transcription now skips silence before the model reads a call, and weighs several possible transcriptions rather than taking the first word that comes to mind. It came out slightly faster than before despite doing more, and on a test call it recovered a whole sentence the previous version had dropped.

Summaries no longer repeat themselves, which happened because the list of points had no real limit. They can also say more: items were capped at five and each one asked to be a single short line, and both of those were being followed at the expense of the content. A long summary in a language that needs more words is no longer thrown away for running out of room.

Recordings were also being quietly degraded on the way in — reducing them to the rate the model expects was adding noise to the speech instead of filtering it out. Outgoing calls were worst affected, because they carry the most of your own voice.

Calls recorded from now on are transcribed with the speaker beside each line.

It is read from the call while it is being recorded — your phone keeps the two sides apart before mixing them together — so it costs no extra time, no extra download and no guesswork. It cannot be done for calls already on the phone, because that information only exists while a call is being recorded.

The two sides start out as Speaker A and Speaker B. Once two outgoing calls agree on which side is which, they become you and the person you were talking to — in the transcript, in what you copy or share, and in the summary.
Any call recorded from now on, in its transcript
Your calls, written out — and summarised

Two big additions, both running entirely on your phone. Nothing is uploaded and both work with no network at all.

Transcription turns a recording into text you can read and search, in fourteen languages. Tap a line to jump to that moment in the call.

Summaries go a step further: what the call was about, what was decided, and what anyone said they would do — with times beside the points that have one, so tapping jumps you straight there.

Each needs a model downloaded over Wi-Fi first; the app tells you what each costs before you start.
Settings ▸ Transcription and Settings ▸ Call summaries
Auto-delete now removes everything it should

If you set recordings to auto-delete, some were quietly kept for ever — the check only looked at recordings CallVault still had a record of, and any it had lost track of were never removed however old they got. On one phone set to keep a week, 131 files had outlived that.

The daily check now reads your recording folders as well, so age alone decides. Only files CallVault named are ever touched, and anything it cannot date is left alone.

Changing the time the check runs also takes effect straight away instead of waiting a day.
Decide what gets recorded, and tidy up recordings

Phone calls and app calls can each record automatically, ask first, or be ignored completely — so \"app calls only\" is now a real setting rather than a combination you had to work out.\n\nRecordings can be shared, and held down to select several at once for sharing or deleting. Deleting a recording kept both on the device and in Drive now asks which copies to remove.
There are no other calls with this number on the phone.
Tick what continues it. Numbers follow the order you tick.
After merging, leave the calls it was made from on the phone as well. Off by default, so a merge leaves one recording. Taking a merged call apart works either way.
It becomes these calls again, each with the transcript and marks it had:
The other calls are removed. Un-merging later brings them back.
The other calls are kept on the phone as well.
